d1_objective: The learner sees a wrong three-tap kernel reproduce a constant-input observation exactly, then sees an impulse probe separate the taps and make a validated convolution fit possible.

targets.lesson_embed_owned_by_lesson_author: <Demo name="EchoKernelLab" caption="Tune the candidate echo kernel on the constant observation, then switch to the impulse probe and validate it." />

implementation_contract.export: default function EchoKernelLab() with no required props
implementation_contract.client_boundary: Put "use client" before imports because the island owns useState and input handlers; keep all constants and pure convolution/error helpers in the same client module.
implementation_contract.lazy_loading: Use the existing explicit registry import promise; DemoHost already constructs React.lazy loaders once at module scope and supplies Suspense, so add no next/dynamic wrapper and do not disable SSR.
implementation_contract.styling: Use existing Tailwind theme utilities and currentColor SVG text/strokes; add no CSS file or global style. Use the house amber #e2903a for observed output and blue #4c8dd6 for the candidate, distinguished by solid versus dashed/hollow marks as well as color.

state.candidate_kernel: number[3] initialized from the Same sum, wrong taps preset

data_and_state.convolution: For n=0..7, y[n] = sum(m=0..2, h[m] x[n-m]). The constant sequence returns 1 for every integer index (steady-state, no startup edge); the impulse returns 1 only at index 0 and 0 otherwise. This states the extension/boundary convention instead of silently treating the displayed record as periodic.

inputs.label: Constant input
inputs.teaching_role: Falsification under the declared observation: an eternal constant input with steady-state-only scoring reveals only h[0]+h[1]+h[2], so distinct kernels with sum 1.05 are observationally identical. A retained startup edge from a finite zero-padded probe would instead expose partial sums and may identify the taps.

inputs.label: Impulse probe
inputs.teaching_role: Validation: the first three output equations have an identity convolution design matrix of rank three, exposing the three impulse-response taps directly and uniquely within the model.

normalized_error.name: normalized L2 output error
normalized_error.zero_output_rule: If both target and prediction have zero L2 norm, define E=0. If the target norm is zero and the prediction norm is nonzero, return a failing nonfinite/infinite sentinel or otherwise force fail; never let the epsilon guard turn that case into a pass.
normalized_error.display: 100*E with two decimal places and a percent sign
normalized_error.pass_source: Always compute the pass error on the impulse probe, even while the constant-input view is selected; also display the currently selected input's error.

pass_rule.recognizable_moment: Readout changes to PASS and states both maximum tap error and impulse validation error; the two output traces coincide within the stated tolerance.

initial_state.visible_result: Observed and candidate outputs overlap at 1.05 with 0.00% selected error, while the status says tap mismatch and explains that the constant input identifies only the sum. This is nonblank and teaches the counterexample before any action.

interaction.input_control: A PresetGroup with Constant input and Impulse probe, wrapped in a role=group region labelled Identification input.
tap_controls: Slider dry h[0], min 0, max 1, step 0.005
Slider early echo h[1], min -0.25, max 0.5, step 0.005
Slider late echo h[2], min -0.25, max 0.3, step 0.005
interaction.preset_behavior: Use a second PresetGroup for candidate kernels; compute activeIndex from all three live values with a 1e-9 comparison and return null after manual tuning.
interaction.feedback: All convolution, errors, active states, SVG geometry, and status text derive synchronously during render; eight samples and three taps require no memoization, effect, transition, network request, or delayed animation.

visual.controls: Two PresetGroups, three Sliders with display values, and one Readout; no hand-rolled buttons, sliders, or live regions.
visual.chart: One dependency-free responsive SVG (viewBox 0 0 480 270, className w-full) with two stacked discrete stem panels: input x[n] above and output y[n] below. Draw observed output as solid amber stems/filled dots and candidate output as dashed blue stems/hollow dots; include in-SVG n axes, numeric y bounds/ticks, panel labels, and a text legend. Derive a shared safe output scale from both traces with fixed padding and a nonzero minimum span so all allowed slider extremes remain finite and visible.
visual.responsive_layout: Stack all content by default; use a one-column grid for sliders and sm:grid-cols-3 above the breakpoint. Let preset buttons wrap. Keep the SVG fluid with no fixed CSS width or horizontal scrolling at 360px.
visual.theme: Axes and labels use currentColor with opacity; semantic text uses text-accent/text-faint and existing theme tokens. Verify light and dark backgrounds.

accessibility.keyboard: PresetGroup supplies native buttons and Slider supplies native range inputs, so Tab, Enter/Space, and arrow-key adjustment work without custom handlers.
accessibility.touch: Existing Button min-h-11 and Slider h-11 provide at least 44px targets; controls remain separated and wrap on narrow screens.
accessibility.aria: Wrap each PresetGroup in a labelled role=group; give each Slider a specific ariaLabel and ariaValueText including the coefficient; use Readout's aria-live=polite for selected error and pass status. Give the SVG role=img and a concise dynamic aria-label naming the selected input, observed array, candidate array, and normalized error.
accessibility.non_color_cues: Solid/filled observed marks, dashed/hollow candidate marks, explicit legend text, and PASS/not yet labels make color unnecessary.

loc_plan.strategy: Keep all fixed vectors and presets as compact module constants; use one three-tap convolution helper, one norm helper, and mapped SVG marks. Store only candidate taps and selected input. Do not add a chart library, reducer, effect, extracted runtime component, CSS module, or utility file.

deterministic_checks: Truth convolved with the constant input is eight copies of 1.05.
[0.90,0.05,0.10] convolved with the constant input is also eight copies of 1.05, so selected error is 0 while maximum tap error is 0.20 and pass is false.
Truth convolved with the impulse is [0.70,0.25,0.10,0,0,0,0,0].
The same-sum wrong kernel has impulse error sqrt(0.20^2+(-0.20)^2)/0.75 = 0.377124, so it fails.
The close preset differs by 0.005 on all taps but has impulse error sqrt(3*0.005^2)/0.75 = 0.011547, proving the tap test alone does not pass.
The threshold preset differs by 0.005 on two taps and has impulse error sqrt(2*0.005^2)/0.75 = 0.009428, so both gates pass.
The exact preset produces zero error and passes; every slider endpoint still produces eight finite samples and a finite percentage.
validation_and_preview: Confirm the component is a default-exported client component, imports only React and @/components/ui, and remains at or below 200 physical lines.
Run npm run validate -- digital-signal-processing impulse-response-and-convolution after the lesson file exists.

Run npm run preview -- digital-signal-processing impulse-response-and-convolution for static lesson light/dark layout; expect the preview command to show a demo placeholder because it deliberately does not hydrate client islands.
Run npm run dev and inspect /courses/digital-signal-processing/lessons/impulse-response-and-convolution at desktop and 360px in light and dark themes.

By hand: keyboard-select every preset/input, arrow each slider at both bounds, verify active preset clears after tuning, reproduce all deterministic percentages, confirm constant zero-error does not pass, confirm Threshold pass does pass, and check that live text and SVG labels neither clip nor rely on color.

checklist_expectation.D1: PASS by the dynamic constant-versus-impulse discrepancy.
checklist_expectation.D3: PASS with the live same-sum counterexample and four named kernel presets.
checklist_expectation.D4: PASS because the learner can falsify uniqueness, switch probes, tune, and receive a two-gate PASS verdict.
checklist_expectation.D5: PASS with one client file, existing UI imports, zero dependencies, and planned 188 LOC.
